domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application — the central aggregate for the leave management workflow. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, manager decision, and optional cancellation.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Value object enumerating the lifecycle states of a LeaveRequest. Governs which transitions are valid.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Drives balance calculations, notice-period checks, and whether manager approval is required.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that governs its rules.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Owns leave balances, submits leave requests, and (when designated as manager) approves or rejects requests from direct reports.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific LeavePolicy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave requests transition to APPROVED or are CANCELLED after approval.

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Notifies employees and managers of leave-related events: submission to manager, approval/rejection to employee, cancellation to both parties.

business_rules: A LeaveRequest transitions only along these edges: DRAFT→SUBMITTED (employee submits), DRAFT→CANCELLED (employee discards), SUBMITTED→APPROVED (manager approves), SUBMITTED→REJECTED (manager rejects), SUBMITTED→CANCELLED (employee withdraws before decision), APPROVED→CANCELLED (employee cancels approved leave). No other transitions are valid. Once in a terminal state (APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED), the request cannot be modified except for the APPROVED→CANCELLED edge. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the requested day count and remainingDays is decremented by the same amount. When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the balance is reversed: usedDays decremented, remainingDays incremented. These balance mutations must be atomic with the status transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Before a LeaveRequest can transition to APPROVED, the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and fiscal year must have remainingDays >= the requested day count. If insufficient, the request must be REJECTED with a reason indicating insufficient balance. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Only an Employee with employmentStatus ACTIVE may submit a LeaveRequest. Employees with status INACTIVE or TERMINATED cannot create or submit leave requests. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

A manager may only approve or reject LeaveRequests for employees who report to them (Employee.managerId === manager's Employee.id). A manager cannot act on their own leave requests. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

When LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is false, a SUBMITTED LeaveRequest auto-transitions to APPROVED without manager intervention. When true, a manager must explicitly approve or reject. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

When LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set, the number of calendar days between the submission date and the LeaveRequest.startDate must be >= minimumNoticeDays. If the notice period is not met, the request must be REJECTED with a reason indicating insufficient notice. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

A LeaveBalance transitions: ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED when remainingDays reaches 0; ACTIVE→CLOSED when the fiscal year ends; EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE when a cancellation reverses a deduction and remainingDays > 0. CLOSED is terminal — no further mutations are allowed against a closed balance. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]
LeaveRequest.startDate must be <= LeaveRequest.endDate. A request with startDate after endDate is invalid at creation time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee must not have two APPROVED LeaveRequests with overlapping date ranges. Before approving, the system must check for date-range overlap with any existing APPROVED request for the same employee. If overlap exists, the request must be REJECTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

The fiscal year for a LeaveBalance is determined by the LeaveRequest.startDate, not the approval date. A leave request spanning a fiscal-year boundary must be split or rejected — a single LeaveRequest cannot consume balance from two fiscal years. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Every state transition on a LeaveRequest (DRAFT→SUBMITTED, SUBMITTED→APPROVED, SUBMITTED→REJECTED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED, DRAFT→CANCELLED) must produce an AuditLog record capturing the entityType 'LeaveRequest', the entityId, the action (mapped to the transition), oldValues (previous status), newValues (new status), performedBy (the actor's employee id), and performedAt timestamp. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, AuditLog appears, not only here]

Emergency leave (leaveType = 'emergency') bypasses the minimumNoticeDays check regardless of the LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays value. The notice-period validation is skipped for emergency leave requests. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest may only reference a LeavePolicy that is ACTIVE (isActive = true). Requests referencing an INACTIVE policy must be rejected at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

A Notification must be created on these LeaveRequest transitions: SUBMITTED → notify the employee's manager (type: LEAVE_SUBMITTED); APPROVED → notify the employee (type: LEAVE_APPROVED); REJECTED → notify the employee (type: LEAVE_REJECTED); CANCELLED (from SUBMITTED) → notify the manager (type: LEAVE_CANCELLED); CANCELLED (from APPROVED) → notify both employee and manager (type: LEAVE_CANCELLED). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Notification appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — the central workflow. DRAFT is the creation state; SUBMITTED awaits manager action; APPROVED/REJECTED are manager decisions; CANCELLED is a terminal withdrawal (from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED).
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — governs whether the policy can be referenced by new LeaveRequests.
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED — ACTIVE while remainingDays > 0 in an open fiscal year; EXHAUSTED when remainingDays hits 0; CLOSED when the fiscal year ends (terminal).
- **Employee**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED — only ACTIVE employees may submit leave.
- **Notification**: PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED — standard notification delivery lifecycle.

## Key domain decisions

- LeaveRequest is the aggregate root; LeaveBalance is a separate aggregate mutated atomically alongside LeaveRequest transitions.
- Balance deduction/reversal is coupled to APPROVED and CANCELLED transitions — never to SUBMITTED or REJECTED.
- Manager approval is scoped to direct reports only; self-approval is prohibited.
- Emergency leave bypasses the minimum-notice-period check.
- Auto-approval when LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is false.
- Fiscal-year boundary crossing is prohibited for a single LeaveRequest.
- Overlapping APPROVED requests for the same employee are prohibited.
- Every state transition produces an AuditLog and appropriate Notifications.

## Open questions for chief architect

Three open questions remain around day-counting semantics, notice-period computation, and overlap definitions — these are genuinely undecided and need human resolution to avoid the BR-001 anti-pattern.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted from startDate and endDate? Is the range inclusive of both boundaries (days = endDate - startDate + 1), exclusive of endDate (days = endDate - startDate), or based on calendar business days excluding weekends/holidays?
open_questions.impact: Affects every calculation that consumes the day count: balance sufficiency checks, balance deductions/reversals, minimum-notice-period validation, and any reporting/analytics on leave consumption. An inconsistent choice across call sites would create the BR-001 anti-pattern.
candidate_options: Inclusive: days = endDate - startDate + 1 (both start and end count as leave days)
Exclusive: days = endDate - startDate (end date is return-to-work day)
Calendar business days: exclude weekends and public holidays from the count

open_questions.question: For the minimumNoticeDays check, is "submission date" the date the request was created (createdAt) or the date it transitioned to SUBMITTED? And is the day count measured as calendar days or business days?
open_questions.impact: Determines when the notice-period validation fires and how it is computed. If submission date = createdAt, a DRAFT created weeks ago and submitted today would always pass. If submission date = the SUBMITTED transition date, the check is meaningful.
candidate_options: Submission date = date of SUBMITTED transition; days = calendar days between submission date and startDate
Submission date = createdAt; days = calendar days
Submission date = date of SUBMITTED transition; days = business days

open_questions.question: For the overlapping-leave check, are adjacent date ranges (e.g., request A ends Friday, request B starts Saturday) considered overlapping?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether back-to-back leave requests are allowed. If adjacent dates are treated as non-overlapping, employees can chain leave requests across weekends. If treated as overlapping, they cannot.
candidate_options: Inclusive overlap: two ranges overlap if startA <= endB AND startB <= endA (adjacent dates do not overlap)
Adjacent-day overlap: two ranges overlap if startA <= endB + 1 AND startB <= endA + 1 (adjacent dates count as overlapping)
